transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Attorney General Todd Blanche is rebuffing questions about investigations into NVIDIA
CEO Jensen Wong.
NVIDIA is a good corporate citizen.
That shouldn't be groundbreaking.
That's something that the president has talked about, that the vice president has talked
about.
Wong resigned earlier this month amid reports.
He'd had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
But President Trump leaned on NVIDIA's board to reinstate his tech adviser as U.S. markets
lost ground.
Trump dismissed criticism that Wong's ties pose a national security risk to the United
States.
An Israeli medical charity says the expansion of Israeli military checkpoints in the occupied
West Bank is preventing Palestinian ambulances from getting to patients and hospitals.
Here's NPR's Lauren Freire.
Violence for Human Rights Israel has published interviews with 25 Palestinian paramedics,
including one who says Israeli soldiers prevented him from reaching a wounded man nearby, leaving
him to bleed to death.
In a new report, the group cites a 350 percent spike in such incidents, including violence
directed at medical workers themselves between 2022 and 2024.
Imran Anati, the report's author, calls this collective punishment.
By blocking an ambulance to evacuate a patient, you're blocking the health care to the whole
Palestinian community.
One Palestinian mayor says six of his residents have died in ambulances delayed at checkpoints
over the past three years.
Asked about the report, the Israeli military told NPR it works to facilitate safe passage
of medical teams, subject to security assessment.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Newly published excerpts from Pope Francis's private diary reveal the late Catholic leader
endured a two year spiritual crisis and believed he had encountered the devil three times in
his life.
Megan Williams has more from Rome.
Flaming eyes, a menacing stare and a raspy voice.
That's how Pope Francis described what he believed were encounters with the devil.
In the newly published book called The Private Diary of Pope Francis, he recounts a spiritual
crisis that began in 2021, eight years into his papacy, where he grappled with how to
wield power over the Catholic Church.
The diaries also reveal his anguish over his handling of the clergy sex abuse scandal in
Chile in 2018.
Longtime friend of Francis Cardinal Victor Fernandez edited the diaries and says the
late Pope considered the spiritual crisis his greatest trial.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
AAA projects 81.5 million people will travel at least 50 miles from home over the Thanksgiving
holiday week in the US.
Rough weather on both the west and east coast could complicate travel.
This is NPR News.
US military officials say the highly toxic lead azide at the munitions plant in Iowa
needs to be detonated in a controlled manner and some residents say they're worried about
the amount of lead particles that could float into the atmosphere with wind gusts that could
travel roughly 100 miles away.
But the Army says the weather conditions for the planned detonation tomorrow morning are
the most favorable.
The superintendent of Grand Canyon National Park is retiring after a scathing report on
a stubborn wildfire last year.
Adrian Scablin reports.
Grand Canyon Superintendent Ed Kiebel made the announcement Monday, more than a week
after a federal report showing that leadership failures and poor communication contributed
to rapid growth and destruction of the Dragon Bravo fire.
That blaze scorched more than 145,000 acres on Grand Canyon's north rim and destroyed
the 100 year old Grand Canyon Lodge.
According to the report, park leaders were disconnected from conditions on the ground
and supported a less aggressive strategy, even as the blaze began to threaten the lives
of park staff.
Kiebel now says he'll step down at the end of the year, citing personal reasons.
Kiebel and the Department of the Interior didn't immediately respond to a request for
comment.
For NPR News, I'm Adrian Scablin in Flagstaff.
Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani is the latest recipient of the nation's highest
civilian honor at the White House today.
President Trump presented his former personal attorney with the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
Giuliani has been among Trump's fiercest 2020 election deniers.
They're listening to NPR News.
